messages:
maria (Infra Ops): Quick update from today's AWS EDP renewal call — wanted to capture the asks and next steps here. Main vendor commitments discussed: preemptible floor guarantees, finer-grained metering, and surge/credit triggers that are evidence-based.

ryan (Head of Cloud): High level: if we can get a hard preemptible floor in region-us-west-2 and instance-level metering, that materially reduces our buffer capacity. :thinking:

sophia (Finance): Can we get a sample pricing ladder and how credits would apply to monthly invoices? Need clarity on reconciliation timing (monthly vs. quarterly).

maria (Infra Ops): Notes I shared on the ask: ```
- Baseline reserved: 500 A100-hours/month (region-us-west-2)
- Preemptible floor: vendor to guarantee >=40% of reserved baseline as non-preemptible or provide equivalent credits when preempted
- Metering granularity: per-instance SKU + timestamped usage lines exportable to CSV/JSON
- Surge credits: automatic credit of 2x usage credit if sustained availability drop impacts >=90th pct of our shifts for >6 continuous hours
```

tom_aws (AWS Account): Thanks for the summary, Maria. We heard those asks. A few clarifying Qs from our side: 1) for the preemptible floor, do you want a hard SLA (with financial clawback) or a contractual credit scheme? 2) for surge credits, what telemetry will you provide as "evidence"? logs, Grafana URL, or signed incident postmortem?

maria (Infra Ops): Prefer a hard credit scheme rather than subjective SLAs — credits tied to measurable metering lines and your availability metrics. We'll provide anonymized Grafana windows + job-run IDs for matching.

elise (Legal): We'll need proposed language for: definition of preemption event, calculation method for credits, and dispute resolution timeline (30 days for invoice disputes). Also want audit rights to usage records under NDA.

ryan (Head of Cloud): Operational constraints: we can accept region-anchored guarantees but want portability if capacity is unavailable (auto-failover to region-us-east-1 with a different credit multiplier). That means routing fallbacks in the contract.

sophia (Finance): Also ask for a cap on retroactive adjustments — can't have open-ended invoice deltas. Propose 90-day lookback window for billing adjustments.

tom_aws (AWS Account): Understood. We can draft a term sheet reflecting: credit scheme, 90-day reconcile window, instance-level metering export. Preemptible floor with credits is doable; hard SLA needs escalation path (ops runbook).

maria (Infra Ops): One more technical ask: ensure metering at 1-min granularity or less for GPU instances. If AWS exposes only hourly aggregates we lose signal.

tom_aws (AWS Account): We'll check feasibility; historically 1-min is heavy but possible via detailed billing/usage reports or partner telemetry.

billing-bot: Invoice case CREATED: INV-4321 — requested: sample billing export for Jan-Mar 2026 to test reconciliation.

elise (Legal): I'll draft an NDA addendum for audit rights and share redlines for the credit calculation clause.

sophia (Finance): Once Tom shares the draft term sheet, I can run the numbers and confirm expected net savings vs. current spot + buffer strategy.

maria (Infra Ops): Action items: @tom_aws send initial term sheet and sample CSV export (by EOD Wed), @elise share NDA addendum draft, @sophia prepare rough ROI model once term sheet arrives. We'll reconvene Thu morning to review. :thumbsup:
